seo.title: Agadir Travel Guide 2026 | Beach, Kasbah, Souk & Hotels | MoroccoTripMap
seo.description: Plan your trip to Agadir: long Atlantic beach, Kasbah viewpoint, Souk El Had, marina, best hotels and resorts, Taghazout and Paradise Valley day trips, and practical tips.
seo.og_description: Beach, Kasbah, souk, hotels and day trips from Agadir — all in one guide.

hero_subtitle: Wide Atlantic bay, modern corniche, hilltop Kasbah views and a gateway to Taghazout surf and Paradise Valley — Agadir is Morocco’s easy beach capital.

overview.title: Welcome to Morocco’s Atlantic Beach Capital
overview.p1: Agadir is Morocco’s big Atlantic beach city — rebuilt after the 1960 earthquake into a wide, modern resort rather than a medina maze. What you get instead is a long sandy bay, a palm-lined corniche, and a hilltop Kasbah that still watches over everything. The pace is slower than Marrakech, sunnier than the north, and built for days that end with salt on your skin and grilled fish on the plate.
overview.p2: Climb the Kasbah at golden hour for the classic curve of the bay. Lose a morning in Souk El Had, one of the largest markets in the country. Use the city as a base for Taghazout’s surf breaks, Paradise Valley’s palm pools, and day trips into the Anti-Atlas. Three to five nights work well if you want beach time without giving up day-trip options.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Agadir
places.subtitle: Beach, Kasbah, souk, marina and the stops that define the city.

beach.title: Agadir Beach
beach.desc: Wide sandy bay for swimming, walking and sunset — the heart of the resort.

kasbah.title: Kasbah (Agadir Oufella)
kasbah.desc: Hilltop ruins with the classic panoramic view over the bay and the modern city.

souk.title: Souk El Had
souk.desc: One of Morocco’s largest covered markets — spices, produce, crafts and everyday shopping.

marina.title: Agadir Marina
marina.desc: Modern harbour with cafés, shops and a pleasant evening stroll by the water.

corniche.title: Corniche
corniche.desc: Seafront promenade of hotels, cafés and beach access along the bay.

birds.title: Valley of the Birds
birds.desc: Small city park with birds and animals — easy stop with children.

taghazout.title: Taghazout
taghazout.desc: Surf village north of Agadir — waves, cafés and a slower coastal vibe.

paradise.title: Paradise Valley
paradise.desc: Palm-lined gorge and natural pools in the hills — popular half-day trip.

crocoparc.title: Crocoparc
crocoparc.desc: Crocodile park and botanical gardens outside the city — family-friendly half-day.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Beach time, city stops and one excursion without rushing.

day1.title: Beach, Corniche & Kasbah
day1.desc: Morning on the beach and corniche, afternoon taxi to the Kasbah for the bay view, evening at the marina.

day2.title: Souk & City
day2.desc: Morning at Souk El Had, afternoon free on the beach or Valley of the Birds, seafood dinner.

day3.title: Taghazout or Paradise Valley
day3.desc: Day trip north to Taghazout for surf vibes, or inland to Paradise Valley. Return for a last sunset on the beach.

directory.title: Where to Stay in Agadir
directory.subtitle: Beach hotels, resorts and a few boutique options near the sea.

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Seafood
eat.subtitle: Beach grills, marina tables and local flavours.

ricks.title: Beachfront seafood
ricks.desc: Grilled fish and simple tables facing the bay — check freshness and prices.

sqala.title: Marina restaurants
sqala.desc: More polished menus and drinks by the harbour.

mounia.title: Local Moroccan kitchens
mounia.desc: Tagines and grilled meats away from pure resort pricing.

cabestan.title: Corniche cafés
cabestan.desc: Juice, coffee and light meals along the promenade.

grande_table.title: Hotel restaurants
grande_table.desc: Reliable options inside larger beach hotels.

table3.title: Near Souk El Had
table3.desc: Simple lunches after a morning in the market.

1.title: Sun protection
1.desc: Agadir is sunny most of the year. Use high SPF, a hat and drink water on the beach and at the Kasbah.

2.title: Stay near the beach
2.desc: Most visitors want easy sand access. Corniche and beach hotels maximise convenience.

3.title: Kasbah by taxi or walk
3.desc: The hill is steep in the heat. A short taxi ride up and a walk down works well.

transport.title: Getting there
transport.desc: Agadir Al Massira Airport (AGA) is the main gateway. Taxis and hotel transfers cover the city; grand taxis for Taghazout.

bargain.title: Souk shopping
bargain.desc: Bargain politely at Souk El Had. Spices, argan and textiles are common buys.

water.title: Swimming
water.desc: Atlantic water is cooler than the Med. Respect flags and local advice on currents.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Agadir
daytrips.subtitle: Surf villages, gorges and classic Souss excursions that fit a single day.

rabat.title: Taghazout & surf coast
rabat.desc: Surf village north of Agadir — reef breaks, cafés and a calmer village pace about 20–30 minutes away.

taghazout.title: Paradise Valley
taghazout.desc: Palm-lined gorge and natural pools in the hills; best with an early start and a driver used to the track.

mohammedia.title: Crocoparc
mohammedia.desc: Crocodile park and gardens south of town — an easy family half-day if you need a break from the beach.

azemmour.title: Essaouira (longer day)
azemmour.desc: UNESCO wind city about 3–3.5 hours north; doable as a long day but better as an overnight if you can.

q1.question: How many days in Agadir?
q1.answer: Three days cover beach, Kasbah and souk. Five days allow Taghazout or Paradise Valley without rushing.

q2.question: Is Agadir only a beach resort?
q2.answer: Mainly yes — the city is modern after 1960. Culture comes from day trips, the souk and the Kasbah viewpoint.

q3.question: Is the beach safe for swimming?
q3.answer: Main sections are popular and often supervised in season. Always follow flags and local advice.

q4.question: Can I visit Taghazout as a day trip?
q4.answer: Yes. Grand taxis and tours run frequently; many visitors go for the day and return to Agadir hotels.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Walk the long sandy beach and promenade; swim if conditions suit, or simply enjoy the Atlantic light.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Explore the large covered market for spices, produce and everyday Moroccan shopping without medina intensity.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Seafood at the marina or a simple dinner along the corniche as the city cools down.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Climb or taxi to the kasbah hill for panoramic views over the bay and new city.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Day trip inland to Paradise Valley pools, or north to Taghazout for surf-town atmosphere.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Back to Agadir for a poolside or beach-area evening — this is a recovery destination as much as a sightseeing one.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Optional Crocoparc for families, or a quieter museum / garden stop in town.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — Free beach or Essaouira road
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Another beach half-day, or start toward Essaouira if continuing the Atlantic route.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last seafood dinner or early rest before onward travel.
